feat(mysql): Allow constraints without names. (#8600)

In MySQL, both `CREATE TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE` syntaxes allow for
`CONSTRAINT`s without names,

```sql
| ADD [CONSTRAINT [symbol]] PRIMARY KEY
      [index_type] (key_part,...)
      [index_option] ...
| ADD [CONSTRAINT [symbol]] UNIQUE [INDEX | KEY]
      [index_name] [index_type] (key_part,...)
      [index_option] ...
| ADD [CONSTRAINT [symbol]] FOREIGN KEY
      [index_name] (col_name,...)
      reference_definition
| ADD [CONSTRAINT [symbol]] CHECK (expr) [[NOT] ENFORCED]
```

This commit adds support for dialects to skip constraint names. Though,
while MySQL will generate a name, there's no attempt to do so here.
